findings.title: Dynamic positional allow_pickle bypasses deserialization gate
findings.desc: The new check rejects the third argument to `np.load` only when it is a truthy `ast.Constant`; code such as `flag = True; np.load(path, None, flag)` passes and permits pickle-driven code execution. This is especially dangerous on the documented resource-limits-only fallback, where runtime confinement is only best-effort.

findings.title: bwrap probe does not cover the real working-directory mount layout
findings.desc: Despite claiming to use the same mounts, the probe omits both `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"` and `--chdir "$PWD"`. If the caller's working directory is beneath `/tmp`, the real run's `--tmpfs /tmp` hides it and `--chdir "$PWD"` fails after the probe succeeds, with no fallback tier attempted.

findings.title: Nonliteral positional allow_pickle bypass
findings.desc: `np.load(path, mmap, variable)` now passes the gate even when `variable` is true, enabling pickle-driven arbitrary code execution; the positional argument should fail closed unless it is provably false, matching the keyword handling.

findings.title: Process guard leaves native execution aliases intact
findings.desc: Patching only `os` and `subprocess` does not patch underlying modules such as `posix`, so a reflection or deserialization escape can still invoke `posix.system`/spawn functions and thereby bypass both process and filesystem-write confinement on non-bwrap tiers.

findings.title: bwrap fails when working directory is under /tmp
findings.desc: The `/tmp` tmpfs hides the caller's working directory when `$PWD` is beneath `/tmp`, yet the real invocation uses `--chdir "$PWD"` without rebinding it; the probe omits this chdir, so it can pass and the actual run then fails.

findings.title: bwrap tier does not block process execution
findings.desc: The bwrap invocation runs Python directly and its namespace/read-only mounts do not prohibit executing binaries, contradicting the later claim that process execution is runtime-blocked and will fail.

findings.title: bwrap probe doesn't match real invocation's `--chdir`/`--ro-bind $AE`
findings.desc: The bwrap probe only mounts `/tmp`,`/dev`,`/proc` and unshare flags, but the real run additionally does `--chdir "$PWD"` and `--ro-bind "$AE" "$AE"`. If the caller's `$PWD` happens to live under `/tmp` (shadowed by the fresh `--tmpfs /tmp`) or is otherwise unreachable inside the sandbox, the probe still succeeds and the real bwrap invocation is chosen, then hard-fails instead of degrading to the unshare/fallback tier — contradicting the stated design goal that the probe "so a present-but-broken userns degrades instead of failing."

findings.title: `_no_exec` error message says "(fallback tier)" but is also used on the unshare tier
findings.desc: `confine.py`'s exec-blocking guard raises `PermissionError("process execution blocked (fallback tier)")` unconditionally, but per the design this same `confine.py` also runs on the "unprivileged unshare -rn" tier, so the error message will be misleading when surfaced to users on that tier.

findings.title: Matplotlib cache scratch dir comment doesn't match bwrap-tier behavior
findings.desc: The comment states `MPL="$AE/mpl"` is "cleaned by the trap", but the bwrap `ENV` hardcodes `--setenv MPLCONFIGDIR /tmp/mpl`, a different path inside the sandbox's own tmpfs (not `$AE/mpl`), so under the bwrap tier the created `$AE/mpl` directory is unused and the comment's cleanup claim doesn't apply to that tier.

findings.title: np.load() allow_pickle gate now fails open for non-literal args
findings.desc: The rewritten check only rejects a truthy 3rd positional arg to `.load()` when it is a literal `ast.Constant`; a variable or expression (e.g. `np.load(f, None, allow_pickle_var)`) is statically accepted. This is inconsistent with the adjacent `allow_pickle=` keyword check, which still fails closed on any non-literal value, so the positional form reintroduces a bypass of the pickle-deserialization RCE gate that the keyword form deliberately closes.

findings.title: Misleading "(fallback tier)" label on shared process-exec guard
findings.desc: `confine.py`'s `_no_exec` PermissionError message is hardcoded as "process execution blocked (fallback tier)", but this same guard is installed and used by both the `unshare -rn` tier and the resource-limits-only fallback tier, not just the fallback. The message will misidentify which sandbox tier actually blocked execution when diagnosing failures.

findings.title: bwrap `--tmpfs /tmp` can shadow `--chdir "$PWD"`
findings.desc: The bwrap invocation mounts a fresh tmpfs over `/tmp` and then explicitly re-binds only `$AE` read-only on top of it (since `$AE` lives under `/tmp`); the new `--chdir "$PWD"` (added to make relative data-file reads work) is not similarly re-bound. If the caller's working directory is itself under `/tmp` (a common case for temp/sandboxed workspaces), the tmpfs mount hides it, so `--chdir` targets a path that no longer exists and the whole bwrap run fails outright — not the "fail cleanly" behavior for moved files described in the doc, but a hard failure for a previously-working CWD.

findings.title: check.py unconditionally executes untrusted code on the host
findings.desc: Because `runpy.run_path()` is called at the end of `check.py`, the untrusted script executes directly on the host during the static checking phase, completely bypassing the OS-level `bwrap` containment. Combined with the removal of `open()` checks, this permits trivial arbitrary file writes to the host (e.g. via `open()` or `pathlib.Path.write_text()`) before the sandbox ever starts.

findings.title: Missing confine.py leaves fallback tier entirely uncontained
findings.desc: The documentation specifies that fallback tiers rely on `confine.py` for Python-level restrictions when `bwrap` is unavailable, but this file is never created or invoked. Execution seamlessly defaults to bare `python3 "$s"`, allowing untethered RCE because process-execution method names were deliberately removed from the AST static gate.

findings.title: AST check for numpy.load fails open for variable arguments
findings.desc: The static gate check strictly expects the 3rd positional argument to be an explicit truthy `ast.Constant` literal in order to trigger a failure. An attacker can effortlessly bypass this limitation and execute unsafe pickle deserialization RCE by injecting a truthy variable (e.g., `allow = True; np.load(..., allow)`).

findings.title: bwrap --tmpfs execution silently shadows PWD if located in /tmp
findings.desc: Binding an empty tmpfs over `/tmp` masks any directory contents beneath it before `$AE` is expressly restored via a subsequent read-only bind. If the caller's active working directory (`$PWD`) is similarly housed within `/tmp`, its local data files are overridden and hidden, rendering legitimate relative data reads functionally broken.

findings.title: Numpy allow_pickle RCE positional check fails open
findings.desc: Changing the static check to require a literal truthy `ast.Constant` creates a trivial RCE bypass; passing a non-constant truthy expression (e.g., `np.load(file, None, 1==1)`) bypasses the `fail()` branch entirely and reaches pickle execution.

findings.title: Runtime write containment misses `open()`, permitting arbitrary host writes
findings.desc: After removing the AST static check for `open()` modes to avoid false rejections, the `check.py` runtime monkeypatch layer only guards `os` functions (like `os.remove`), failing to mock `builtins.open` or `io.open`; this leaves the fallback tier trivially vulnerable to unabated arbitrary host file creation (e.g., `open('~/.bashrc', 'w').write(...)`).

findings.title: `bwrap --chdir "$PWD"` crashes if executing from inside `/tmp`
findings.desc: The bwrap sandbox mounts a fresh tmpfs over `/tmp` before resolving `--chdir "$PWD"`. If the caller invokes the script from a working directory currently inside `/tmp`, that directory gets shadowed out of existence, causing bwrap to crash with "No such file or directory".

findings.title: `np.load` static check bypass for pickle RCE

findings.title: Native arbitrary file write via unrestricted `open()`
findings.desc: The static check limiting `open()` to read-only modes was removed, relying entirely on runtime containment. However, `check.py` executes the script natively (via `runpy`) before any OS sandboxing is applied and does not mock `open` or `pathlib` writes, enabling unrestricted file overwrite on the host.

findings.title: Missing network exfiltration protections in fallback tier
findings.desc: The design states that network egress is blocked at runtime in all tiers, but `check.py` (which acts as `confine.py`) does not mock network modules like `socket`. Un-sandboxed network requests (e.g. via `pandas` over HTTP) remain entirely unblocked during native checking and in the fallback tier.

findings.title: `bwrap` execution fails if `$PWD` is within `/tmp`
findings.desc: The `bwrap` container mounts `--tmpfs /tmp` immediately before attempting `--chdir "$PWD"`. If the caller's working directory is located within `/tmp`, the tmpfs effectively hides it, causing `--chdir` to fail and completely breaking execution.
